title: Final Hour Runway Log
body:
Purpose: personal runbook for the solo operator window (final hour before launch). Use as tick-list + quick comms templates + rollback triggers. Not a canonical runbook — this is my micro-checklist and timestamps so I don't forget tiny things when things start moving fast.

T-minus timeline (local timezone):
- T-60 (60m): sanity check infra + pager path, set alarms. Confirm pg_auto_failover disabled for schema migrations.
- T-45: warmup critical services (warm-up script: scripts/warmup/critical.sh) — watch heap, GPU init logs.
- T-30: run smoke tests against staging infra and prod-mirror (small subset): smoke/stage-smoke.sh --short.
- T-15: final env var check, secrets in place, verify KMS key active.
- T-05: announce in #releases and #engineering-ops, set status page maintenance mode if needed.
- T+00: cutover -> run release script (release/cutover-run.sh) with dry-run flag off.
- T+5..+30: live validations, watch latency/5xx, errors. Keep one minute per validation batch.

Quick checklist (tick off):
- [ ] Gate PR merges: ensure only REL-8467 & REL-8421 are in.
- [ ] Backports applied: REL-8421 -> release/1.8; REL-8467 -> release/1.8-hotfix.
- [ ] DB migration: migration/20260310_add_kv_index.sql applied to canary DB (run: DB_CANARY_URL).
- [ ] Feature flags: ffctl set inference.experimental=false for prod.
- [ ] KMS: key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd active and rotation off.
- [ ] Autoscaler policy: set min replicas = 2 for serving-runtime-prod.
- [ ] Observability: tracing enabled (env OTEL_ENABLED=true), retention hooked up.
- [ ] Slack pings queued for comms.

Backport notes (quick):
- REL-8421: small nonce fix. Cherry-pick: git cherry-pick -x f3c2e1a -> branch release/1.8. Run unit tests locally (make test-unit).
- REL-8467: quantization default fix for aarch64. Manual compile on aarch CI required. Patch link: PR 1764.

Quick commands to keep handy:
- rollforward: ./release/cutover-run.sh --commit $COMMIT_SHA --env prod
- rollback (fast): ./release/rollback.sh --to-tag v1.8.3 --force
- check errors: kubectl -n prod logs -l app=serving-runtime --since=10m | grep -i error | head -n 50
- quick CPU/GPU check: scripts/infra/instance-health.sh --region us-west-2

Comms snippets (copy/paste):
- pre-cutover (T-05): "Heads-up: final runway in 5m for release REL-8421/REL-8467. Expect ~5-10m of low-impact deploy. Paging path unchanged. If you see >1% 5xx, ping me @ava and escalate to #sre."
- post-cutover success: "Cutover complete. Key checks: smoke OK (short), no increased 5xx, traces flowing. Rolling out canary -> full in 30m unless issues."
- rollback alert: "Rolling back to v1.8.3 due to elevated errors. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate. ETA 10m for rollback completion."

Escalation contacts:
- Oncall (SRE): Jordan Patel (@jordan) — pager: +1-415-555-0123
- Infra lead: Riley Chen (@riley) — slack DND off during window
- Product EM: Mina Kapoor (for customer comms)

Validation checks (first 30m):
- [ ] 200/latency check: endpoint /health returns 200 <200ms for 95th pct
- [ ] Sample inference: run scripts/validate/sample_infer.py against prod-key (limit 5 queries) -> verify no token-level regressions
- [ ] Billing spike check: console > billing > last 10m (look for sharp token cost rise)
- [ ] Metrics: request_rate stable, queue_depth <= 3

Non-tech reminders (so I don't forget):
- water bottle next to me
- 10m stretch at T+20
- set phone to vibrate but not DND—need Slack alerts

Open questions / TODO after cutover (notes to self):
- run regression eval with prompt-set A (place results into Confluence page REL-8467-regress)
- follow up with model-onboarding team about kernel selection logs (they requested samples)
- add a small note in the official runbook about the KMS flakiness observed last week

If anything odd: capture full logs (kubectl -n prod logs --all-containers --since=1h) and upload to: https://storage.redwood-internal/release-logs/REL-8467/$TIMESTAMP

End of log — will timestamp each major action below during the window. Keep this file minimal and linear so I can paste sections into the final incident note if needed.
